taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: stoutish, erect, leafy stems 4-15(-20) cm. high.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: stems 4-15(-20) cm. high.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: perennial from a thickish, short-branched caudex or lignescent rhizomatous base.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 474, Antennaria: mainly white-woolly, dioecious perennials.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: with erect tufts of basal leaves.

traits.cauline_leaves.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: cauline leaves lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, becoming sessile and moderately reduced above.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: basal leaves 2-6(-10) cm. long including the petioliform base.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: basal leaves 2-14 mm. wide.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: basal leaves linear-oblanceolate to oblanceolate or obovate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 474, Antennaria: leaves mostly entire.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: densely gray-lanate-tomentose.

traits.stem_hairs.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: densely gray-lanate-tomentose.

traits.hair_colour.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: gray-lanate; grey-white in the photos; sRGB by eye.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: heads 6-12, in a close umbelliform cyme or terminal glomerule: drawn as a rounded corymb.

traits.inflorescence_outline.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: a close umbelliform cyme or terminal glomerule.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the cluster of heads 1.5 cm to 3 cm across, as in the photos.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: heads 6-12.

traits.capitulum_kind.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 474, Antennaria: heads mostly several to numerous, discoid.

traits.involucre_height_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: pistillate involucres campanulate, 5-8 mm. high; the staminate shorter and broader.

traits.involucre_diameter_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: involucres 5 mm to 8 mm across, about as broad as high, as in the photos.

traits.disc_colour.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: phyllaries mostly greenish at base, the outer dark brown or blackish green, the inner usually with whitish tips; the heads read creamy white with dark flecks in the photos; sRGB by eye.

traits.sexual_system.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 474, Antennaria: mainly white-woolly, dioecious perennials.

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: achenes glabrous.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 478, Antennaria lanata: July-Aug.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: achenes ripe August and September.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: dense tufts of erect, narrow, grey-woolly leaves, some sending up short woolly stems capped by a tight cluster of creamy, dark-flecked heads. The basal leaves' petiole share is set by hand from the leaf and petiole lengths the traits give, as no rule sets a rosette leaf's.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for woolly pussytoes from its sources and the photos the traits cite: the herb program's structure (stems, nodes, basal leaves, how the flowers are borne). Its inflorescence is drawn as one cluster at each stem's tip, sized by the traits, so the stem ends where the cluster begins. The rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.1 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
